description: Repeated authentication attempts against a single account until one succeeds, evidenced by a run of consecutive login failures concentrated in a short window from the entity's own known device.
A login from a geographic location physically unreachable from the entity's previous session within the elapsed time, indicating a stolen or shared credential used from a second location.
Automated login attempts using credential pairs leaked elsewhere, evidenced by a failed login paired with an unfamiliar device rather than the sustained single-device hammering of brute force.
Access to a resource well outside the entity's normal and peer-department resource set, especially a sensitive resource reached via an improbable resource transition — a compromised account pivoting.
A session presenting a device identity inconsistent with the entity's known devices — mismatched fingerprint, or an unfamiliar OS/MAC pairing — indicating identity masquerading.

Sustained, deliberately unhurried access to sensitive or diverse resources — a long session and broad resource diversity without the burstiness of brute force, designed to stay under rate-based detection.
A gradual, multi-session broadening of a known entity's behaviour — rising privilege and resource footprint across successive profile versions rather than one sharp spike.
Flagged as anomalous by Phase 4, but no known attack signature scored above the minimum match threshold — warrants manual triage rather than an automated category.
